speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; could you tell me how long it has been there and if you have any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The patient's history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and a lesion that started as an ulcer with a history of trauma (ant bite) despite no signs of infection strongly suggests this neutrophilic dermatosis. The mention of anterior uveitis and prior steroid use also aligns with the systemic inflammatory nature of the condition, which often presents at sites of skin trauma (pathergy).
